title: Ideals, quotient rings, and polynomial quotients
terms: ideal; quotient ring; prime ideal; maximal ideal; irreducible polynomial; comaximal ideals.

exposition.text:
An ideal I in a commutative ring R with identity is an additive subgroup with rI ⊆ I for every
r ∈ R. The quotient ring R/I has cosets as elements and inherited addition and multiplication.
A proper ideal is prime precisely when R/I is an integral domain, and maximal precisely when
R/I is a field. Every maximal ideal is prime; the converse need not hold.
Over a field F , the quotient F [x]/(p) for nonconstant p has vector-space dimension deg p, with
representatives of smaller degree. It is a field exactly when p is irreducible. Arithmetic reduces
powers using p(x) = 0 in the quotient. A polynomial quotient may have zero divisors or nilpo-
tents even though F [x] itself is a domain.
A proper ideal is prime when ab ∈ I forces a ∈ I or b ∈ I, and maximal when no proper ideal
lies strictly between it and R. A nonconstant polynomial is irreducible over a field when it has
no factorization into two positive-degree polynomials. In F [x]/(p), a class f is a unit exactly
when gcd(f, p) = 1. Ideals I, J are comaximal if I + J = R; the Chinese remainder theorem then
identifies R/(I ∩ J) with R/I × R/J. A nilpotent element has some positive power equal to zero.

solution.text:

Factor x + x = x(x + 1) over F . A representative of degree below 3 is invertible iff it is

this requires c = 1 and a + b = 0, leaving two possibilities.

In R = Q[x]/(x − 2), what is the inverse of the class of 1 + x?
(A) 1 − x (B) x − 1 (C) (1 − x)/3 (D) (1 + x)/3 (E) It has no inverse.

solution.text:
2 2
In this quotient x = 2. Thus (1 + x)(x − 1) = x − 1 = 1. Equivalently rationalize with the
conjugate: (1 + x)(1 − x) = −1, so the inverse is x − 1.

question.text:
2
Which ring is isomorphic to R[x]/(x − 1)?
2
(A) R[x]/(x ) (B) R (C) C (D) Z × Z (E) R × R

solution.text:
The ideals (x − 1) and (x + 1) are comaximal, so the Chinese remainder theorem gives a
product of their quotients, each isomorphic to R. Explicitly, send a polynomial class to
(p(1), p(−1)).

question.text:
Which polynomial p makes F [x]/(p) a field with sixteen elements?
2
4 2 4 4 4 3 2 4
(A) x + x + 1 (B) x + 1 (C) x + x (D) x + x + x + 1 (E) x + x + 1

solution.text:
A degree-four polynomial over F is irreducible iff it has no linear factor and is not divisible
2
2 4
by the only monic irreducible quadratic x + x + 1. For x + x + 1, neither zero nor one is a
2 2 2
root, and reduction modulo x + x + 1 gives remainder one. The first choice is (x + x + 1) ;
the others have a root zero or one. The irreducible quotient has dimension four over F ,

hence sixteen elements.
